questions.question: "Reserve Bank of India" is listed in the __________ list given in the Seventh Schedule in the Constitution of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Union__

 
• Reserve bank of India, being a central banking facilitator in the country, will definitely be the part of the Union government, as this ensures clarity of jurisdiction and avoid competing claims. That’s why it is listed in the union list of the seventh schedule of the Indian constitution.
 
• The central bank of India is The Reserve Bank of India (RBI). It was set up on April 1, 1935, under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• The basis of the establishment of RBI was the recommendations given by a Committee known as the ‘Hilton Young Commission’ set up by the then British Government in India.
 
• It started as a private bank with private shareholding as was in vogue in most foreign central banks of the world operating at that point in time.
 
• When RBI was set up, its capital was fixed at Rupees 5 crore i.e. Rupees 50 million).
 
• When the RBI was set up, it took over the functions of currency issues from the Government of India and the power of credit control from the then Imperial Bank of India.
 
• Initially, RBI had its headquarter in Calcutta (now Kolkata) but soon shifted its headquarter to Bombay (now Mumbai) in 1937.
 
• However, from January 1, 1949, RBI was nationalized by the Government via an Act known as the Transfer of Public Ownership Act, 1948.
 
• The RBI Act covers the whole of India in terms of supervision, control, and guidance/directions to financial entities in India.

questions.question: In females, the ovaries are located ______ on each side of the lower abdomen.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **One**

__**Explanation:-**__

 
• In females, the ovaries are located in the pelvic cavity, typically **one** on each side of the lower abdomen.
 
• They are situated near the lateral walls of the pelvis, adjacent to the uterus and fallopian tubes.
 
• While the exact position can vary slightly among individuals, the ovaries are generally positioned below the level of the pelvic brim, in close proximity to the iliac vessels and the ureters.
 
• They are connected to each other via a fallopian tube and produce ovum- egg, which travels down the uterus via this tube.
 
• These ovaries also secrete hormones known as estrogen and progesterone that play a role in menstrual cycle and fertility of a woman.

questions.question: _________ can give the Union parliament power to make laws on matters included in the State list.

options.text: Securities and Exchange Board of India

questions.solution: It’s the upper house of the parliament, i.e. Rajya Sabha which can give the union parliament power to make laws on matters related to state list. This provision is mentioned in Article 249, and involves not less than 2/3rd members of the house to pass a resolution for enabling parliament to legislate over state list.

questions.question: The method of soil conservation in which ploughing is done parallel to the contours of a hill slope to form a natural barrier for water to flow down the slope is called?
questions.solution:
The method of soil conservation in which ploughing is done parallel to the contours of a hill slope to form a natural barrier for water to flow down the slope is called __**Contour ploughing.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d75abffb1d7f21a0cb21fc40907655c03b3b6a401e1a3b03d94c609e009dc398.png] 

 
• It’s the contour ploughing which involves digging the field parallel to the contours of a hill slope.
 
• This measure checks soil erosion, as they create water break which prevents the formation of gullies and rills during the heavy downpour.
 
• Also, it allows the infiltration of water in the ground, which recharges ground water levels.

questions.question: Through photosynthesis at least a half of the total carbon dioxide fixation on earth is carried out by?
questions.solution: It’s the algae which performs at least half of the total carbon fixation on earth. Carbon fixation means conversion of inorganic carbon to organic compound by living organism. On other hand, algae refers to Aquatic organisms which has the ability to do photosynthesis.

questions.question: The salt concentration (measured as salinity in parts per thousand), is _______ % in sea.
questions.solution: The salt concentration is 3.0-3.5% in sea, which can also be expressed as 35 parts per thousands. This implies that in 1000g of sea water, 35g would be salts. These salts are predominantly Sodium and chloride. Moreover, because of this sea water is denser than fresh and pure water.

questions.question: Locust, Butterfly, Scorpion and Prawn are all examples of which Phylum?
questions.solution: It’s the phylum Arthropoda that Locust, Butterfly, Scorpion and Prawn belong to. Moreover, phylum refers to a taxonomic classification which is ranked ‘class’ but below ‘kingdom’. Arthropoda, on other hand, refers to invertebrate animal having an external skeleton, a segmented body and paired jointed appendages.

questions.question: The ________ balance is the sum of the balance of merchandise trade, services and net transfers received from the rest of the world.
questions.solution: It’s the current account that reflects the balance of good and services and net transfer received from the rest of the world. Moreover, the purchase of goods and machineries, investment made, are part of capital account. Thus it’s both the capital and current account together that constitute Balance of payments, which is the record of a country economic transaction done with the rest of the world.

questions.question: Around how much percent of earth’s surface is covered with water?
questions.solution: Around 3/4th of the earth surface i.e. 70-80% is covered with water and rest is the land area. However, water is also present in air as water vapors, in the form of moisture in soil and is also an important element in varied living beings. Additionally, of the total water area, 96.5% is present in the form of ocean.

questions.solution: Sher khan defeated Humayun at Chausa in 1539 and kanauj in 1540, resulting into Humayun’s fleeing to Iran. Sher khan was an ethnic Pashtun, and established Sur Dynasty. However he died an accidental death in 1545 and was succeeded by his son, Islam Shah.

questions.question: If an object moves in a circular path with uniform ________, its motion is called uniform circular motion
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e __**Speed**__

 
• For the** uniform circular motion to be there, uniform speed is required. **
 
• The reason why we don’t use velocity over speed is the fact that velocity is direction based, whereas speed means the movement of an object at a certain rate and is thus taken into account direction.
 
• **And in the given question, since the direction is constantly changing, we would use speed.**
 
• 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eb04ec9797808e6bb147499ecb1af0e7ec231e2440591959e86e91ab056c2923.png] 

 
• **T**he distance is not always equal to the displacement in a uniform circular motion.
 
• In a uniform circular motion, an object moves along a circular path with uniform speed.
 
• Due to a circular path traveled the distance will be greater than zero but the displacement can or cannot be zero.
 
• The displacement is In UCM is called as angular displacement.
 
• Velocity is always perpendicular to the radius.

questions.question: Vinegar and Baking Soda together produce ____________.
questions.solution: Vinegar and Baking soda together produces carbon dioxide. The reason being that baking soda is sodium bicarbonate and is a basic compound, and Vinegar is an ascetic acid, thus when the two combine chemical reaction takes place, and due to the acidic nature of vinegar, elements of carbon and oxygen are released. Thus forming CO₂. .

questions.question: Which of the following is the second highest civilian award of India given for exceptional and distinguished service in any field including service rendered by government servants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Padma Vibhushan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Padma Vibhushan is the second-highest civilian honor in India.
 
• The award is given for exceptional and distinguished service without discrimination of distinction of race, occupation, position, or sex. 
 
• Padma Awards, which were instituted in the year 1954 and is announced every year on the occasion of Republic Day.
 
• Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian award in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Padma Bhushan for distinguished service of a high order.
 
• Padma Shri for distinguished service. 
 
• Param Vir Chakra is the highest gallantry award.
 
• Ashoka Chakra is the highest peacetime award.

questions.question: The reflection formed by the plane mirror is ________________.
questions.solution: Reflection formed by the plan mirror is called Lateral inversion. This means, upon reflection via a Plane mirror, right hand side of an objects appears to be on left in the image formed and left side of an object appears on the right hand side.

questions.question: In April 2017, who was made United Nation's Messenger of Peace?
questions.solution: It is Malala Yousafzai who was made the United Nation’s Messenger of peace. She is a Pakistani activist and had also won the Nobel Prize for Peace in 2014 which made her the youngest recipient of this award.

questions.question: The relation between the consumer’s optimal choice of the quantity of a good and its price is very important and this relation is called the ________ function.
questions.solution: It’s the demand function which tends to establish the relation between consumer’s optimal choice and price relation. In other words, it helps to elaborate that how many units of a good will be purchased by a consumer at different prices.

questions.question: According to the categories of land mentioned in the Chola inscriptions ___________ was known as the land of non-Brahmana peasant proprietors?
questions.solution: It is Vellanvagai which is termed as the land of the non-Brahmana peasant proprietor during Cholas time. This dynasty dates back to 3rd BCE, and lasted till 13th century CE. Prominent rulers belonging to it are RajaRaja chola and his successor Rajendra chola.

questions.question: In Microsoft Excel, the ______() function is used to count the number of cells within a range that meet the given criteria.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __COUNTIF__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• Excel **COUNTIF function** is used for** counting cells **within a **specified range** that meet a certain criterion. For instance, one can write a COUNTIF formula to find out how many cells in one’s worksheet include a number greater than or less than the number that has been specified. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• Use **COUNTIF**, one of the statistical functions, **to count the number of cells** that meet a criterion; for example, to count the number of times a particular city appears in a customer list.
 
• In its simplest form, COUNTIF says:
 
 
• 
 
=COUNTIF(Where do you want to look?, What do you want to look for?)

 
 
 
 
• For example:
 
 
• 
 
=COUNTIF(A2:A5,"London")

 
 
• 
 
=COUNTIF(A2:A5,A4)
